exposure: previous cesarean section history (leading to VBAC attempt)
outcome: cervical dilatation rate during active labor
duration of the second stage of labor
rate of prolonged second stage of labor
cohort: The study included 13,983 primiparous and 736 secundiparous women attempting their first VBAC, all with term singleton pregnancies in spontaneous labor resulting in vaginal delivery.
finding: Women attempting their first VBAC experienced a significantly faster active phase of labor progression and a shorter second stage compared to primiparous women.
mod_finding: Women at their first VBAC, following a previous cesarean section, demonstrated a faster active phase progression and a shorter second stage of labor compared to primiparous women delivering vaginally.
birth_weight: N/A (VBAC group had higher neonatal birth weight compared to primiparous group)
